meta.title: Correlations from officially sourced numbers, with n
meta.rule: A correlation is published only if both variables come from an official source for the same units, and only with n and a confidence interval. Where the official overlap is too small or does not exist, the value is blank and the reason is stated.
meta.confidence: 95% interval on r via Fisher z.

rows.correlation: team points for vs points against (2026, n=32 teams)
rows.note: Both columns are official standings columns. A strong team necessarily pairs high PF with low PA, so this is descriptive, not a signal.

rows.correlation: team wins vs point differential (2026, n=32 teams)
rows.note: Point differential travels between seasons better than wins do; this is the 2026 snapshot.

rows.correlation: point differential persistence (2025 to 2026, n=32 teams)
rows.note: The 2026 value is a part-season (8-9 games); a full-season persistence figure cannot be computed until the season ends and is not inferred. The 2025 season is 17 games.
Wins are compared across unequal game counts (17 vs 8-9), which flatters the correlation; the ratio is not rescaled because rescaling would be an inference.

rows.correlation: QB passing yards vs WR1 receiving yards (same player)
rows.note: The two official leader tables describe different players, so they cannot be paired into one observation. The statistic the project needs is a per-team-game join of a quarterback's passing yards and his top receiver's yards; the official season-leader pages do not publish that join and the official team pages do not expose it in a machine-readable form. Published as blank rather than replaced with the committed third-party figure.
rows.needed: Per-game official passing and receiving lines for the same games, for a large enough sample to estimate r.
